READABILITY.evidence: Names and doc comments are mostly clear. However, business logic uses single-letter names for important values: `t := &decodedShapeIndex{...}`, `d`, and `p`/`l` in the decode helpers. That hurts scanning in a 500-line file. The cap applies.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: shapeindex_encode.go is 502 lines, over the 500-line cap. It ignores the project conventions: it adds its own tags (`shapeIndexTagPolygon`...) instead of the existing typeTag values, and puts every per-shape codec in one file instead of next to each shape. decodeShapeIndex is about 95 lines.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Every length is bounded before allocation, and allocations grow in chunks via `min(n, decodeChunkSize)`. Shape IDs, edge IDs, cell order and overlap are all validated. EOF becomes ErrUnexpectedEOF. The target index stays unchanged if decoding fails, and Encode holds RLock. Truncation and fuzz tests cover this.

C7-11-CASE1.evidence: The change is purely additive: two new files. No existing typeTag values, per-shape wire formats or Shape interface methods were changed. New tags are local to the ShapeIndex format.
